description.en-US: The bill this allocation belongs to. Immutable: moving an allocation between bills would change both bills' totals, and BR 36's invariant is checked per bill.

The order line whose value this allocation carries. Unique with the bill: one order line contributes at most one allocation row to any one bill, so a split that gave the same line to a bill twice would be refused by the database rather than by a check somebody could forget.
How much of the order line's quantity this bill settles. A split apportions the line's quantity across bills, and the sum across every bill of the order equals the line's ordered quantity.

This bill's share of the order line's net. Allocated with the same D-04 algorithm the combo components and the fixed vouchers use - one implementation, because the hard part is identical and getting it subtly different in each is how a total stops adding up.

This bill's share of the order line's tax. Allocated rather than recomputed, for the same reason the bill's tax_total is: a per-bill recomputation would not sum back to what the order was actually charged.

What this allocation contributes to the bill's total. Stored rather than derived from net plus tax, because it is the figure the BR 36 invariant is checked on and a derived value would have to be recomputed identically at every check site.
